sentences.text: Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Sandeep Tripathi Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Raj Beer Singh,J.
1. Supplementary affidavit filed by learned counsel for the applicant is taken on record.
2. Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the entire record.
3. The present second bail application has been filed by the applicant in Case Crime No. 528/2017 (S.T. No. 182/2017), under Sections - 376, 506 IPC & 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station - Kandhla,
District - Shamli with the prayer to enlarge the applicant on bail.
The first bail application of applicant was rejected by the co-ordinate Bench of this Court, vide order dated 21.11.2019.

Monu vs State Of U.P. on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27513774/
1 3.
It has been argued by learned counsel for applicant that applicant is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in this case.

The informant has lodged first information report on 28.08.2017 against applicant alleging that applicant was physically exploiting his minor daughter, due to which his daughter tried to commit suicide by putting herself on fire.

Learned counsel submitted that the allegation that applicant has physically exploited the victim is wholly false and in fact victim has suffered burn injuries at her chest and abdomen due to some dispute with her father.
It has been shown that statement of victim has already been recorded before the trial court as P.W.-2, wherein she did not support the prosecution version and turned hostile.

In her statement before the trial court, she has stated that a quarrel has taken place with her father and she sustained burns while she was preparing food and that applicant-accused has not done anything against her.
She has further stated that applicant has not committed any rape upon her nor he has done anything forcibly.

Victim was declared hostile and she was cross examined from the side of prosecution but she did not make any statement against the applicant and she has also denied her statement under Section - 164 Cr.P.C.
The age of victim is stated about 16 years.

Lastly, it was submitted that applicant is languishing in jail since 29.08.2017 and the statement of informant and victim have already been recorded before the trial court and thus there is no possibility of tampering with evidence.

It was stated that there are number of formal witnesses, who are yet to be examined and thus trial of the case would take sufficient long time, whereas the applicant-accused has already undergone the detention of about six and a half years.
5. Learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for bail but it could not be disputed that during trial victim has not supported the prosecution version and turned hostile.

6. Considering the submissions of learned counsel for the parties, facts of the case, nature of allegations, period of custody and all attending facts and circumstances of the case, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, a case for bail is made out.
Hence, the present second bail application is hereby allowed.

7. Let the applicant - Monu involved in the aforesaid crime be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two local sureties each of the like amount to the satisfaction of court concerned subject to the following conditions:
i. The applicant will not tamper with the evidence during trial.
ii.
The applicant will not pressurize/intimidate the prosecution witnesses.
iii. The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.
iv. The applicant will not try to contact, threat or otherwise influence the complainant or any of the witness of the case.
8. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the trial court shall be at liberty to cancel the bail of applicant in accordance with law.

Order Date :- 15.2.2024 S Rawat  Monu vs State Of U.P. on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27513774/
